title: Colder winter minimum temperatures did not decrease the next-year growth of mountain pine beetle tree-mortality area in four western US regions, 1999-2025
abstract: Question: do cold winter extremes decrease the next-year growth of mountain pine beetle (Dendroctonus ponderosae) tree-mortality area when survey effort, outbreak size and host depletion are controlled? Approach: we wrote the plan before we opened the data. We gridded USFS Insect and Disease Detection Survey maps (1997-2025; Regions 1, 2, 4 and 6) onto 0.5-degree cells and used only cells with at least 25% survey-footprint cover in both years. We compared log growth of mortality area from survey year t to t+1 with the coldest daily minimum (CPC Tmin) of the brood winter, with cell and region-by-year fixed effects, outbreak size, the previous five years of mortality, and CRU summer rain and heat. Intervals come from a bootstrap over survey years. Result: in 3,986 cell-year pairs (378 region-cells, 26 year pairs), a 10 C colder winter minimum changed log growth by +0.007 (95% interval -0.283 to +0.208). This excludes a halving of growth. The coefficient was negative in only 2 of 4 regions and in 1 of 2 periods. A lead-winter placebo (+0.030) was as large as the test winter, and a threshold model (minimum at or below -30 C) gave +0.039 (-0.309 to +0.329). Spruce budworm, a negative control, also gave no clear effect. The model detected density dependence and host depletion. A secondary term for October-November cold was negative (-0.45; -0.90 to -0.01), but it was positive in one region and its placebo was also negative, so it is only a hypothesis. Limitations: gridded air temperature is not phloem temperature; aerial survey methods changed; the test covers year-to-year variation, not the long-term release of outbreaks into formerly cold places. Code, plan, derived grids, results and figures are bundled; CRU data stay external.

display.caption: Change in log growth of mortality area per 10 C colder winter minimum, with 95% bootstrap intervals over survey years. Blue rows are pre-declared and gray rows are exploratory. The dashed line marks a halving of growth. The primary pooled estimate is +0.01 (-0.28 to +0.21).

(a) Mountain pine beetle tree-mortality area mapped by USFS aerial surveys in four regions, 1997-2025 (log scale). (b) Percentage of the 370 analysed 0.5-degree cells with a winter minimum daily Tmin at or below -30 C (CPC data), winters 1992-2025.

Binned partial regression of residual log growth on residual coldness after cell and region-by-year effects and controls (20 quantile bins, 95% intervals of bin means). (a) Winter minimum, pre-declared primary exposure: no slope. (b) October-November minimum, secondary exposure: a negative slope that did not pass the placebo and regional checks.

citations.reason: Weed et al. (2015) found no broad-scale link between winter minima and beetle dynamics in 1997-2010 aerial survey data; we find the same in 1999-2025 with survey-footprint, host-depletion and placebo controls.
